skill.name: consent-registry
skill.description: Records pseudonymous opt-ins, lawful-basis evidence, withdrawals, complaints, hard bounces, restorations, and erasure tombstones through an append-only consent registry.
skill.summary: Maintain auditable consent evidence and immediate suppression state for pseudonymous subscribers.
skill.author: aaron-he-zhu

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are Markdown formatting, repository links, metadata URLs, or a safe fixed Git command. The skill does invoke a repository Python utility and permits broad deny-only suppression, creating bounded execution and integrity risks.

remediation.issue: The suppression path allows any validated producer to change contact eligibility.
remediation.suggestion: Enforce tenant and subject scope, authenticate producers, rate-limit suppression events, and alert on unusual suppression volume.

remediation.issue: The query workflow invokes a script selected through AARON_SKILLS_ROOT.
remediation.suggestion: Resolve and verify the trusted root, pass subject IDs as literal process arguments, and reject unexpected script ownership or permissions.

content.user_title: Manage Consent and Live Suppression Records
content.value_statement: Consent evidence and withdrawal state often become inconsistent across marketing systems. This skill records pseudonymous events and checks authoritative suppression status before contact.
actual_capabilities: Records opt-in events with source, timestamp, lawful basis, proof references, and expected revision.
Queries live suppression state by replaying the authoritative consent event stream.
Applies immediate suppression for unsubscribes, complaints, and hard bounces.
Validates restoration against fresh evidence that is newer than the withdrawal.
Processes verified erasure while retaining a suppression tombstone.
Regenerates per-subject views from accepted event projections.
limitations: Requires the shared root runtime, schema, catalog, and registry script for canonical changes.
Does not send email or synchronize an email service provider.
Does not score send readiness or build audience segments.
Accepts pseudonymous subject identifiers and proof references, not raw contact details.

use_cases.title: Record Verified Opt-In
use_cases.description: Capture a subscriber opt-in with timestamp, source, lawful basis, and proof references.

use_cases.title: Enforce Immediate Suppression
use_cases.description: Record an unsubscribe, complaint, or hard bounce before any later eligibility check.

use_cases.title: Review Consent Evidence
use_cases.description: Inspect lawful-basis records, pending proposals, restorations, and erasure status for a pseudonymous subject.

prompt_templates.title: Record an Opt-In
prompt_templates.prompt: Record opt-in for subject [ID] using [source], [timestamp], [basis reference], and [proof reference]. Report missing evidence.
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner records one verified subscription.

prompt_templates.title: Apply a Suppression
prompt_templates.prompt: Immediately suppress subject [ID] for [unsubscribe, complaint, or hard bounce] using event [event ID]. Confirm the live result.
prompt_templates.scenario: An operator handles a safety event.

prompt_templates.title: Assess a Restoration
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess whether subject [ID] can be restored using fresh evidence [reference] dated [timestamp]. Compare it with the latest withdrawal.
prompt_templates.scenario: A specialist validates a new subscription after withdrawal.

prompt_templates.title: Process Erasure and Audit State
prompt_templates.prompt: Process verified erasure for subject [ID] using request [reference]. Preserve suppression, regenerate projections, and report event offsets and verification results.
prompt_templates.scenario: A privacy lead completes an advanced erasure workflow.

output_examples.input: Check suppression status for subject sha256-7d9f.
output_examples.output: Subject sha256-7d9f is suppressed. The live replay result overrides cached segment data. Next action: exclude the subject from contact.

output_examples.input: Record opt-in without a basis or proof reference.
output: Lawful basis remains unknown and no proof is on file.
Provide a trusted basis reference and proof reference.

output_examples.input: Erase a verified subject and report the result.
output_examples.output: Projected consent details were removed. A suppression tombstone remains active, and the verification query confirms the subject is not eligible for contact.

best_practices: Use only pseudonymous subject identifiers and minimum proof references.
Check live suppression before every eligibility or send decision.
Require trusted host capabilities for opt-in, restoration, and erasure changes.
anti_patterns: Do not store email addresses, names, phone numbers, or raw identifiers.
Do not clear withdrawals using older evidence or inferred consent.
Do not edit event streams or projection files manually.

faq.question: Can this skill send email?
faq.answer: No. It records consent and suppression facts. Sending and provider synchronization are separate workflows.

faq.question: What identifier should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide one pseudonymous subject ID from your system. Do not provide raw email, phone, name, or address data.

faq.question: Which record is authoritative?
faq.answer: The append-only consent event stream and its replay query are authoritative. Projection files are caches.

faq.question: Can an unsubscribe wait for review?
faq.answer: No. A validated unsubscribe, complaint, or hard bounce must create immediate suppression.

faq.question: When can suppression be restored?
faq.answer: Restoration requires trusted authorization and opt-in evidence with a timestamp later than the latest withdrawal or erasure.

faq.question: Does a standalone installation update canonical state?
faq.answer: No. Without the verified shared runtime, it can only prepare a proposal or safety handoff.
